candidate.answerReason: The diameter makes angle AOC equal to 130 degrees, and equal radii make triangle AOC isosceles, giving angle CAB equal to 25 degrees.

methods.label: Use the equal radii
methods.explanation:
Because \(AB\) is a diameter, \(A,O,B\) lie on a straight line with \(O\) between \(A\) and \(B\). Thus
\[
\angle AOC=180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ.
\]
The radii \(OA\) and \(OC\) are equal, so triangle \(AOC\) has equal base angles. Its angle sum gives
\[
\angle CAO=\frac{180^\circ-130^\circ}{2}=25^\circ.
\]
The rays \(AO\) and \(AB\) coincide, so \(\angle CAB=\angle CAO=\boxed{25^\circ}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
methods.levelReason: This route uses only the diameter definition, equal radii, and elementary triangle-angle facts.

methods.label: Use the inscribed angle theorem
methods.explanation:
The central angle \(COB\) intercepts the minor arc \(CB\). Since \(A\) is diametrically opposite \(B\) and \(\angle COB=50^\circ\), \(A\) does not lie on this minor arc. Thus the inscribed angle \(CAB\) intercepts the same arc as \(COB\).

An inscribed angle is half the central angle intercepting the same arc, so
\[
\angle CAB=\frac12\angle COB
=\frac{50^\circ}{2}=\boxed{25^\circ},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
methods.levelReason: The inscribed angle theorem is standard school geometry within AMC 10 scope.
